prerequisites: Basic knowledge of Laplace, Zeta, and Fourier transforms

learning_outcomes.text: Provide students with the basics of mathematical modeling of natural and/or artificial continuous and discrete-time systems.
Provide students with techniques for analyzing systems described by input-state-output and input-output mathematical models, with particular reference to linear and stationary systems.
Provide students with the main techniques for analyzing feedback systems.
Introduce students to the use of main software for system analysis and simulation.
Students will acquire methodological tools to describe simple engineering systems using an adequate mathematical model.
Students will learn to derive small-signal models of non-linear systems.
Students will be able to characterize the time response and main structural properties of linear systems.
Students will be introduced to the main techniques for analyzing dynamic systems, both in the time domain and in the complex domain.
Students will learn about the analysis of systems in the frequency domain, presenting the main parameters that characterize linear systems in this context.
Students will be able to analyze block diagrams, deriving an overall model, and evaluate the response of this model to given signals.
Students will be able to analyze the structural properties of such a model, with particular reference to stability.
Students will be able to use Matlab/Simulink software for system analysis and simulation.

syllabus_topics: Review of matrix algebra: elementary operations on matrices and vectors. Eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a matrix. Vector spaces. Banach spaces and Hilbert spaces. p-norms of matrices and vectors.
Dynamic systems: input, state and output variables, state and input-output representations, classification of dynamic systems.
Elements of modeling, examples of mathematical models.
Non-linear systems: equilibrium points of a non-linear system, linearization around a trajectory and an equilibrium point.

Analysis of linear and stationary continuous and discrete-time systems: the principle of superposition of effects, free evolution response and forced response. Calculation of the transition matrix through diagonalization. Natural modes.

Analysis of linear and stationary continuous-time systems using the Laplace transform: transfer function, impulse response and step response, characteristic parameters of the step response, response to polynomial and sinusoidal signals, steady-state and transient response.
Analysis of linear and stationary discrete-time systems using the Zeta transform: transfer function, impulse response and step response, steady-state and transient response.

Stability of equilibrium points: simple and asymptotic stability, instability. Examples of stability analysis of equilibrium points of non-linear systems (pendulum, etc.). Notes on Lyapunov Theory. Stability of linear systems, Routh criterion, application of Routh criterion to discrete-time systems. Input-output stability of linear systems.
Interconnected systems and block diagrams: series, parallel and feedback systems. Representation of interconnected systems. Notes on the stability of interconnected systems.
Realization theory for single-variable systems, canonical observability form and canonical reachability form.
Digitization techniques for a continuous-time system. Sampled-data systems: sampler and ZOH filter. Sampled-data representation of a finite-dimensional linear system.
Fourier series and transform. Frequency response of a linear and stationary system.
Filtering action of dynamic systems: low-pass, high-pass, band-pass, notch filters.
Stability analysis of closed-loop systems: Nyquist diagram plotting, Nyquist criterion. Stability margins.
Structural properties: reachability, controllability and observability, Kalman canonical forms.
Matlab and Simulink for the simulation and analysis of dynamic systems.
teaching_methods: Class exercises using MATLAB/SIMULINK (20% of total hours)

assessment_methods.method: Discussion of project work (simple assignments in Matlab/Simulink)

assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written test and an oral interview. The written test verifies the student's ability to calculate the response of a linear system to given signals, plot Bode diagrams, and analyze the stability properties of interconnected systems. The oral interview, which follows the written test, consists of a discussion on the theoretical topics covered in the course and on simple Matlab/Simulink assignments, in order to ascertain the acquisition of concepts and content. Passing the written test is a prerequisite for access to the oral test, but it is not sufficient to pass the exam.
bibliography: G. Celentano, L. Celentano – “Modellistica, Simulazione, Analisi, Controllo e Tecnologie dei Sistemi Dinamici - Fondamenti di Dinamica dei Sistemi”, Vol. II, EdiSES, 2010.
Other texts and/or notes suggested by the lecturer.
